sentences.text: The facts that emerge for consideration are that respondent No.1 filed a claim case under Section 166(1) of the MV Act claiming compensation to the tune of Rs. 3,40,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a motor accident on 10.03.2020.

The accident occurred when the applicant along with one Chhamesh Kumar Sahu was coming to his village Kanker from village Mudkhusra by his motorcycle bearing registration No. CG-19- BF-1642 at about 10:30 in the night near village Govindpur.

Non- applicant No.1 came from the backside on his Bullet motorcycle bearing registration No.
CG-19-BD-8411 (hereinafter called 'offending vehicle') and dashed the motorcycle driven by the applicant/respondent No.1, by which they fell down and the applicant sustained injuries.
The applicant was admitted to the Govt. Komaldev District Hospital, Kanker from 10.03.2020 to 12.03.2020.
The applicant sustained a fracture on his left leg.
The treatment of the applicant was continued.
He was aged about 70 years on the date of the accident and was earning Rs. 6,000/- per month from agriculture.
On account of the accident, he became permanently disabled and unable to perform his work.

He claimed Rs.1 Lakh on account of medical treatment, conveyance, special diet and assistance, Rs.50,000/- for future medical treatment, Rs.50,000/- towards loss of income during the treatment, Rs. 1 Lakh on account of permanent disability, Rs. 20,000/- for loss of pain and suffering, Rs.20,000/- towards loss of better life expectancy and thus the total amount of Rs.
3,40,000/- was claimed in the claim case.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19138 3)

The non-applicants/respondents No. 2 & 3 filed their reply to the claim application filed by the applicant before the Tribunal and submitted that the accident occurred by dashing of two vehicles and therefore the principle of contributory negligence is applicable in the case.

The driver, owner and the Insurance Company of the motorcycle bearing registration No. CG-19-BF- 1642 which was being driven by the applicant, were not made a party in the case, and therefore, for the reason of non-joinder of the necessary parties, the claim application was liable to be dismissed.

In their written statement, they also submitted that on the date of the accident, non-applicant No. 1 had a valid and effective driving license and his motorcycle was duly insured with the Insurance Company/non-applicant No. 3.
If the Tribunal comes to the conclusion that the applicant is entitled to any amount towards compensation, the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation amount.

4) The non-applicant No.3/Insurance Company also filed its written statement and submitted that the owner, driver and the Insurance Company of the motorcycle which was driven by the applicant were also necessary parties and without impleading them in the claim case, the same is not maintainable on the ground of non-joinder of necessary party.
The accident occurred on account of the negligence of the applicant himself.
The applicant and non-applicants No. 1 & 2 are relatives and only to get compensation, they collided with each other and filed a false claim case before the Tribunal.

It is also submitted that the father Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19138 of the applicant is an Assistant Sub Inspector at Police Station Kanker and with the collusion of the Investigating Officer; he involved the motorcycle of non-applicant No. 1 in the accident.

On the date of the accident, the driver of Bullet Motorcycle bearing registration No. CG-19-BD-8411 did not have a valid and effective driving license and thereby there was a breach of policy condition thus, the claim case was liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: In support of the claim case filed by the applicant, he filed a final report of the criminal case filed against non-applicant No.1, FIR, spot map, property seizure memo and MLC report as Ex.P/1 to Ex.P/4.

With respect to the treatment of the applicant, he filed documents Ex. P/5 to Ex. P/6,
medical bills Ex. P/8 to P/16, special diet Ex.P/17 to P/36 and examined himself as PW-1 to prove the documents filed by him.
6) After considering oral as well as documentary evidence led by the parties, the Tribunal partly allowed the claim application of the applicant and awarded the compensation amount as mentioned in para-1 of this judgment.
Hence this revision.
7) Learned counsel for the non-applicant No.3/ Insurance Company would argue that the award passed by the Tribunal is erroneous and contrary to the law applicable to the facts of the case.
The driver of the offending vehicle did not have a valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident and there is a breach of the policy conditions.
There was an inordinate delay in lodging FIR after the accident which smells false implication of the motorcycle of non-applicant No. 1.

The police did not forward Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19138 any information to the Insurance Company as soon as the information was received about the accident as provided under Section 158(6) of the MV Act.
The accident occurred due to the applicant's own negligence which dashed with the cattle on the road.
The applicant/respondent No. 1 is contributory negligent in the accident.

He would further submit that the applicant is the nephew of non-applicant No. 2 and cousin brother of non- applicant No. 1 and thereby they hatched a conspiracy to get compensation from the Insurance Company.

He would also submit that the interest part as also the compensation awarded are on the higher side that too without proving the medical bills and injuries by examining the treating doctors therefore the revision may be allowed and the impugned award may be set aside.
8)
On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent/non-applicant No. 1 would oppose the submissions made by counsel for the applicant.
9) I have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the records with utmost care and caution.

10) The non-applicant No. 3/ Insurance Company has pleaded in his written statement that non-applicant No. 1 did not have a valid and effective driving license on the date of the accident and thereby there is a breach of the policy condition.

To prove their contention that there is a breach of policy condition; non- applicant No.3/Insurance Company has not examined any witness in their support that the driver of the offending vehicle Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19138 was not having any valid and effective driving license on the date of the accident.
There is no ground in the revision filed by the Insurance Company that there is a breach of any of the policy conditions so they may be absolved from their liability.
While deciding the claim case filed by the applicant, issue No. 5 was framed by the Tribunal regarding breach of policy condition, if any.

While deciding issue No. 5, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that a breach of any of the policy conditions has not been proved by the Insurance Company and thereby, the issue regarding breach of policy condition is set at rest.

3 11)

So far as the other grounds of contributory negligence are concerned, no evidence was led by non-applicants No. 1 & 2 or even by non-applicant No.3/Insurance Company that the applicant was negligent in any manner at the time of the accident so that it can be held that there was a contributory negligence.

Since the contributory negligence is not proved by the non-applicants,
there is no necessity for the applicant to implead the owner, driver and the insurer of the vehicle driven by him and to claim against his own vehicle.

12) In the case in hand, issue No. 2 has been decided by the Tribunal by considering the evidence led by the applicant i.e. the final report, Ex.P/1, FIR, Ex.P/2 in which the report has been made against non-applicant No. 1 for rashly and negligently driving his motorcycle, and therefore, it cannot be said that the applicant was also negligent in driving his vehicle.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19138 13)

The other grounds raised by the Insurance Company are that the police have not intimated about the accident as provided under Section 158(6) of the MV Act and therefore a forged claim case has been made by the applicant.

Although Section 158(6) of the MV Act provides for information regarding any accident involving death or bodily injury to any person is recorded by the police, the officer in charge of the Police Station shall immediately forward a copy to the Tribunal, however,
non-compliance with the same would not be fatal for the applicant in view of the fact that it is a beneficial legislation, the applicant admittedly received injuries in the accident and remedy to file a claim case under Section 166 of the MV Act is also available to the applicant.
Therefore, even if the Insurance Company is not informed by the police, that itself would not create any doubt that no accident occurred or the applicant has filed a fake claim case.
The applicant has filed a duly constituted claim application supported with documentary evidence on the basis of which the Tribunal has awarded compensation amount to the applicant.

14) Further, there is no bar to file a claim application by the applicant even if the non-applicants are his relatives because it is a case where the accident occurred and the applicant received injuries irrespective of the fact that the offending vehicle was owned or driven by his relative or any other person.

15) The further argument of the Insurance Company is that the Tribunal has awarded the amount of compensation on the very higher side without there being any examination of the treating Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19138 doctor.
The Tribunal has considered the injuries received by the applicant and also the expenses incurred towards medicines, conveyance, special diet etc.
The disability certificate was not filed by the applicant and in the absence of the examination of the doctor; no amount of compensation has been awarded towards permanent disability.

The Tribunal has awarded Rs. 6,144/- towards medical bills produced by the applicant which was incurred by him during treatment, a total of Rs.40,000/- on account of conveyance, special diet, nursing assistance and pain and suffering, Rs.6,000/- was awarded towards loss of income during treatment and, thus,
the tribunal has awarded the total compensation of Rs. 52,144/-, which, by no stretch of imagination, can be said to be either exorbitant or on the higher side looking to price index and cost of living and also the expenses towards treatment.

The amount awarded is just and proper and therefore the revision filed by the non-applicant No.3/Insurance Company being devoid of merit deserves to be and is hereby dismissed.
No costs.
